svg.title: Animated MRI scanner hardware and working-principle diagram
svg.desc: A detailed educational schematic showing the superconducting magnet, liquid-helium cryostat, shim and gradient coils, radiofrequency coils, patient at the scanner isocenter, the five steps from proton alignment to Fourier image reconstruction, and simplified MRI physics equations. Animated lines show cryogenic circulation, radiofrequency excitation, gradient encoding, returning tissue signals, and data flow.

g.text: Plain-language journey with engineering detail — proton alignment, resonance, spatial encoding, relaxation, and reconstruction
Layers around the patient and the magnet centre (isocenter)
Outer → inner: cryostat • superconducting magnet • shims • gradients • RF body coil • bore
• NbTi coils in liquid helium (4 K)
• Common fields: 1.5 T or 3 T; always on
• Transmit coil sends B₁ radio pulses
• Close receive coils capture faint echoes
• Shims + room shield cut radio noise
Safety: magnet stays ON — screening is essential.
Repeated many times with different gradient settings to build each slice or 3D volume
In plain words: hydrogen protons behave like tiny magnets and line up with the strong field.
Engineering: a slight spin excess creates net magnetization M₀; spins precess at f₀.
In plain words: a radio pulse at exactly the right pitch tips the tiny magnets sideways.
Engineering: B₁ at f₀ = (γ/2π)B₀ rotates M by the selected flip angle.
In plain words: small magnetic slopes give each location a signal pitch and timing code.
Engineering: Gz selects a slice; Gy phase-encodes; Gx frequency-encodes.
In plain words: protons settle back at tissue-dependent speeds and broadcast faint radio echoes.
Engineering: T1 recovery and T2 decay shape the FID/echo induced in receive coils.
In plain words: the computer decodes all the coded echoes and turns them into detailed pictures.
Engineering: samples fill k-space; inverse FFT converts spatial frequencies to pixels.
Position changes local field and frequency
Bandwidth + Gz set slice thickness Δz
kx grows while Gx is on; ky steps with Gy
Centre of k-space: contrast; edges: detail
Biosynex Atlas educational diagram — simplified; real MRI systems and pulse sequences vary.
